source.author: verg
source.text: Interea magnum sol circumvolvitur annum, et glacialis hiemps aquilonibus asperat undas.
source.text_original: Interea magnum sol circumvolvitur annum, / et glacialis hiemps aquilonibus asperat undas.
source.text_english: Meanwhile the sun completes the great year, and icy winter roughens the waves with the north winds.

reuse.author: hier
reuse.text: Quod autem ait: Girans girando vadit spiritus, et in circulos suos revertitur, sive ipsum solem spiritum nominavit, quod animet, et spiret, et vigeat, et annuos orbes suo cursu expleat, ut ait poeta: Interea magnum sol circumvolvitur annum: et alibi: Atque in se sua per vestigia volvitur annus; sive quod et lunae lucentem globum et astra Titania: Spiritus intus alit: totamque infusa per artus Mens agitat molem, et magno se corpore miscet; non de annuo solis cursu, sed de quotidianis semitis ejus loquitur.
reuse.text_original: Quod autem ait: Girans girando vadit spiritus, et in circulos suos revertitur, sive ipsum solem spiritum nominavit, quod animet, et spiret, et vigeat, et annuos orbes suo cursu expleat, ut ait poeta: Interea magnum sol circumvolvitur annum: et alibi: Atque in se sua per vestigia volvitur annus; sive quod et lunae lucentem globum et astra Titania: Spiritus intus alit: totamque infusa per artus Mens agitat molem, et magno se corpore miscet; non de annuo solis cursu, sed de quotidianis semitis ejus loquitur.
reuse.text_english: But in saying, Girans girando vadit spiritus, et in circulos suos revertitur, he either called the sun itself spiritus, because it gives life, breathes, lives, and completes the yearly cycles by its course, as the poet says: Meanwhile the sun revolves the great year; and elsewhere: And the year turns back upon itself in its own tracks; or because he also said of the moon’s shining globe and the Titanian stars: Spiritus intus alit: totamque infusa per artus Mens agitat molem, et magno se corpore miscet; he is speaking not of the sun’s yearly course, but of its daily paths.
